title: Status Review Proof Due Date on Military Service Holds: Calculation Clause
content:
**Clause — Hardship and Protective Holds.** The current proof of active military duty asked for before a status review of a running Military Service Hold is due on the last day of the upcoming review's overdue window: the days allowed for the status review proof run from the day of the request to the due date of the status review that next falls due, reviews falling due every review interval counted from the hold's start date, plus the tier's review overdue days. For the status review proof, a review falling due on the day of the request counts as already fallen due, so the review the proof is for is the following one. The status review proof due date never falls after the hold's current end date; where the count would carry it past that date, the due date is the current end date. The days allowed for the status review proof are a whole number of calendar days and are not rounded.

## Inputs

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| Start date and current end date | The hold's record |
| Review interval and review overdue days | The Military Service Hold's figures in the product's status review calendar |
| Day of the request | The day the request is made |

## Worked examples (hypothetical; interval 90 days and overdue days 30, as the calendar sets for this tier)

Start date 1 January; reviews fall due on 1 April, 30 June and 28 September.

- **Request on 10 June, current end date 28 December.** The next review falls due on 30 June, 20 days away. Days allowed: 20 plus 30, that is 50; due date 30 July, before 28 December, so 50 stands.
- **Request on 10 June, current end date 15 July.** The count of 50 would reach 30 July, after 15 July. The due date is 15 July and the days allowed are 35.
